pl-l4d35c1-d1e115.summary: States that though the Lord allows the husband to dismiss his wife for fornication, the same license is not taken from women.
claims: Wives too may separate for fornication.

pl-l4d35c1-d1e118.summary: Quotes Jerome: the Lord commanded that a wife not be dismissed except for fornication and, if dismissed, remain unmarried; whatever is commanded to men applies equally to women, for an adulterous wife is not to be dismissed and an adulterous husband kept.
claims: The law of separation applies equally to both sexes.

pl-l4d35c1-d1e127.summary: Adds Jerome: with us what is not lawful for women is equally not lawful for men, and the same service is judged by equal condition.
claims: Men and women are bound equally.

pl-l4d35c1-d1e134.summary: Concludes that a woman can sue her husband for fornication as a man can his wife.
claims: A wife can accuse her husband of fornication.

pl-l4d35c1-d1e137.summary: Quotes Pope Innocent: Christianity condemns adultery equally in both sexes; but women do not easily accuse their husbands, while men more freely bring adulterous wives before priests; so communion is denied to women whose crime is revealed, while men's hidden sins are not easily punished on suspicion, though they would be excluded if found out.
claims: Adultery is equally condemned in both sexes.
Unequal enforcement arises from unequal accusation.

pl-l4d35c1.summary: The permission to dismiss a spouse for fornication applies to wives as well as husbands: Jerome says what is commanded to men applies to women, and an adulterous wife is not to be dismissed while an adulterous husband is kept; so a woman can accuse her husband of fornication as he can her. Innocent: Christianity condemns adultery equally in both sexes, though women rarely accuse their husbands, so men's hidden sins go unpunished.
claims: Husband and wife have equal right to separate for fornication.
Adultery is equally condemned in both sexes.
